To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the accuracy of written-recall performance is superior for a method of presentation in which the learner is required to integrate visual and oral input (dual method) and for explicated learning material.
the accuracy of written-recall of the learning material improved in the order of simple oral, visual, dual, and that explication of learning materials improved recall accuracy.

(a) retention of a complex sequence of information is better for dual presentation than for simple oral presentation, (b) the accuracy of written free-recall of the sequence is better for dual and visual equal-time presentations than for simple oral presentations, and (c) the accuracy of recall is better for an explicated than for a non-explicated sequence, regardless of presentation mode.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of the following variables on written recall: method of presentation, explication of material, and internal consistency of the material.
the effects of the complexity of presentation and the internal consistency of learning material on accuracy of written recall.
the effects of the complexity of learning material presentation on retention.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the more complex the method of presentation and the more explicated the learning material, the greater will be the retention.
dual presentation is superior to visual equal-time presentation which is in turn superior to simple oral presentation.
retention of learning material presented by the dual method is superior to retention by either the visual equal-time or simple oral methods, but inferior to retention by the explicated method.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the more complex the method of presentation, the greater the accuracy of the written recall.

the accuracy of written-recall performance is a function of the internal consistency of the learning material, and that the dual method of presentation is the least effective of the three for this measure of retention.

dual and visual presentation are better than oral, but that the superiority of visual over dual presentation depends upon the complexity of the presentation and upon the degree of explication in the learning material.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of visual aids in the classroom can improve learning outcomes.
, in general, dual mode presentation is better for recall.
the dual method is the most efficient way to present learning material. (Author/AM)
